transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (ZenWave - Head of Platform), Jason Lee (ZenWave - Security Eng), Amir Khan (ZenWave - CTO)

Summary: quick product walkthrough focused on request telemetry, configurable retention toggles, logging redaction and PII masking in the Redwood Console and via API. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for fraud-detection chat assistants; main concerns: PII, audit logs, and egress for EU customers.

Topics: console demo, API flags, retention policy examples, KMS integration, SOC2/ISO requests, performance impact of redaction, shared artifacts: https://redwood.ai/s/retention-controls-deck, docs.redwood.com/security

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hi everyone, thanks for joining. can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Priya: yep loud and clear, thanks. we are excited to see the retention stuff today.
[00:10] Maya: great, quick agenda — luca will demo the Console toggles and the API flags, then i’ll cover security/compliance docs and next steps. feel free to interrupt.
[00:20] Amir: perfect. our primary ask is how we can prevent storage of PII in request logs, but still keep useful telemetry for debugging and monitoring. also curious about cost implications.
[00:33] Luca: absolutely. we’ll start in the Console. i’ll share my screen now — *screen share starts* — ok, do you see the Console nav?
[00:40] Jason: yes, seeing it. the retention settings look familiar but walk us through the toggles.
[00:45] Luca: so top-level: Request Storage Mode with three options — Store Full, Store Redacted, and Ephemeral. Store Full is for dev sill for debugging, Store Redacted applies configured redaction rules server-side, Ephemeral retains only short-lived K/V session caches for the inference runtime and nothing persists to object storage.
[01:05] Priya: and redaction rules — are they regex-based? or ML-based?
[01:09] Luca: both. you can apply regex patterns, dictionary lists, or the redwood PII classifier. we recommend regex + classifier for high-sensitivity fields. note that classifier has a small inference cost, we typically see ~5-7% token overhead on request processing when you enable full PII detection.
[01:27] Maya: important to call out — the classifier runs inline before persistence; it doesn't affect the model scoring path. latency delta is usually sub 20ms on our hosted tier but we can run a dedicated benchmark for you.
[01:38] Jason: 20ms is ok for most flows, but for fraud detection we have sub-100ms SLO. do you have batching or KV cache options that help?
[01:46] Luca: yes, we have workload-aware batching and KV caching. the Console's Optimize tab suggests a config for low-latency streams — e.g. smaller batch size and prefix KV caching to avoid recomputing tokens. redaction runs post-tokenization stage so caching still helps.
[02:05] Amir: can we route certain requests to a dedicated pool to guarantee latency?
[02:09] Maya: that's Redwood Dedicated — you can pin model variants and routes. we can put fraud-critical routes on dedicated to hit your SLOs and keep other traffic on hosted.
[02:16] Priya: about audit logs — we need immutable audit trails showing who changed retention policies and when. is that in the Console?
[02:23] Luca: yes, Console audit logs capture policy changes, user, IP, and a diff. we can retain audit logs for configurable windows; longer retention is an add-on. audit logs are write-once and stored in encrypted object storage with KMS.
[02:36] Jason: speaking of KMS — do you integrate with our cloud KMS or support HSM?
[02:41] Maya: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault and customer HSMs via PKCS#11 for Private deployments. on hosted we offer envelope encryption. we’ll include the KMS integration guide in the artifacts.
[02:55] Priya: will that satisfy our compliance? we need SOC 2 + ISO attestation — do you have docs?
[03:01] Maya: yes, SOC 2 + ISO documentation is available — we’ll send the attestation and a compliance FAQ in the follow up.
[03:07] Jason: great. i want to understand the difference between Console redaction and API-side redaction flags — which is authoritative?
[03:13] Luca: Console sets the account defaults. API calls can override per-request with headers: X-Redwood-Retention: ephemeral|redacted|full. if a policy is enforced at account level (like required_redaction=true), the API cannot relax it. so Console can enforce guardrails.
[03:29] Amir: what about PII that’s embedded in base64 or obfuscated? will the classifier catch that?
[03:34] Luca: it's tricky. classifier handles patterns and common encodings; we also provide a 'pre-process' hook where you can register a server-side transform to normalize inputs before redaction. for obfuscated strings we recommend a custom regex or preprocessor.
[03:48] Priya: can you show an example of the redaction preview? i want to see how names and account numbers get masked.
[03:53] Luca: sure — switching to the Preview panel. here’s a sample request: "Hi, my card 4111-1111-1111-1111 and email priya@zenwave.com". Preview shows: "Hi, my card <REDACTED_CARD> and email <REDACTED_EMAIL>". you can adjust tokens preserved, e.g. last4.
[04:12] Jason: nice. is the redaction deterministic? we need stable hashes for linkage but without storing raw PII.
[04:19] Luca: we offer deterministic hashing using a customer-provided salt stored in your KMS. hashed values are stable, non-reversible, and can be used for linking events. we don’t store the salt in plaintext.
[04:30] Priya: regarding request telemetry — we need to keep latency histograms and per-route error rates but not the full prompt. what does Redwood send to metrics?
[04:37] Maya: by default we emit aggregated telemetry: p50/p95/p99 latencies, token counts, error codes. you can toggle token-level telemetry on or off. full request bodies are only kept if you select Store Full.
[04:50] Amir: okay. what's the expected storage reduction if we choose redacted vs full?
[04:55] Luca: it depends on prompt shape, but typical customers see 60-85% reduction in storage volume when they redaction rules strip PII and long-instruction sections. we also compress stored payloads.
[05:09] Priya: can we set different retention periods per route? e.g., fraud route 7 days, support chat 90 days.
[05:16] Luca: yes, per-route retention is supported. you can also set an override to keep only aggregated metrics for certain routes.
[05:23] Jason: what about regulatory data residency — we have EU customers whose requests must not leave eu-west-1. can we lock storage region?
[05:31] Maya: yes, you can pick storage region per-subscription; Private / VPC deployments can be on-prem or in-region. Hosted supports region locking when requested for enterprise accounts; we'll need to set that up in the contract.
[05:44] Amir: any network egress controls? we prefer no egress to third-party analytic vendors.
[05:49] Luca: we don't forward raw requests to third parties by default. integrations (like analytics or Sentry) require explicit enablement and a bucket ACL. you can disable all external integrations from the Console.
[06:02] Priya: can you demo the API header override quickly? we want to see code for toggling ephemeral storage.
[06:07] Luca: yep — switching to API examples. sample curl: 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" 
  -H "X-Redwood-Retention: ephemeral" 
  -d '{"prompt":"...", "model":"rw-v1"}'

Luca: that header will short-circuit persistence and only keep ephemeral runtime state. if account-level enforcement is set, the server will return 403 when an attempt is made to set ephemeral against a locked policy.
[06:39] Jason: does ephemeral affect embeddings or vectors created on the request?
[06:43] Luca: embeddings are separate — by default we don't persist embeddings unless you call the embeddings endpoint with storage enabled. for combined flows you can set per-endpoint policies.
[06:54] Maya: quick question on costs — what is the delta on storage cost if we keep redacted vs ephemeral?
[06:59] Luca: redacted is still stored in S3 and billed per GB; ephemeral is not stored long-term so you avoid storage charges but still pay compute. ballpark — redacted storage cost varies with retention window, but customers typically save 30-70% on storage line items vs full retention. we can produce a cost model for your traffic patterns.
[07:20] Priya: perfect — we'd like a model. i will share sample traffic shapes.
[07:24] (short pause, background noise)
[07:30] Luca: jumping back to the Console, under Security > Keys we show KMS integrations; here you can configure envelope encryption, and choose salt management for deterministic hashing. we also support per-tenant key rotation scheduling.
[07:45] Jason: rotation — does rotation affect ability to link hashed PII across rotations?
[07:50] Luca: if you rotate the salt without migrating hashes, linkage will break. we support a migration workflow where the old salt is kept wrapped and we rehash or maintain mapping tables for a transitional window. this is described in the KMS guide.
[08:05] Amir: do you support RBAC for who can change retention policies? we need separation of duties.
[08:10] Maya: yes — roles: admin, security, devops, auditor. you can set policy change permissions to a role and enable SSO via SAML. there’s also an approval flow for policy changes with email notifications.
[08:23] Priya: any chance to export the audit logs to our SIEM?
[08:27] Luca: yes, audit logs can stream to your SIEM via secure syslog or push to an S3 bucket behind your account. we have built connectors for Splunk and Datadog.
[08:37] Jason: curious about the performance hit of streaming audit events synchronously — is that async?
[08:41] Luca: audit streaming is async; it won't block inference. we persist events locally with guarantees and then push to your sink.
[08:49] Priya: will the exported logs contain redacted request bodies? we need to ensure PII doesn't leak into SIEM.
[08:55] Luca: by default export respects the account retention policy; if you choose redacted storage the exported payloads will be redacted. you can also configure masking rules specifically for exports.
[09:07] Amir: are there built-in evals to detect regression when enabling redaction? i.e., changing redaction rules could change model outputs and harm accuracy.
[09:14] Maya: great point — Redwood Optimize has a small eval harness where you can run a prompt set through different redaction configs and measure MRR/accuracy delta. we can attach your prompt set to run a regression check during rollout.
[09:29] Jason: will that eval include latency and token counts as metrics?
[09:33] Luca: yes, the eval reports latency, token usage, and output diffs. it’s part of the rollout canary in the Console.
[09:42] Priya: let's talk exceptions — sometimes support teams need access to full logs for troubleshooting. how do you handle just-in-time unredaction or escrowed access?
[09:51] Luca: we support a JIT access flow where an authorized auditor can request a time-limited unredaction. the request is logged and multi-approval is required. the unredacted payload is delivered in a sealed S3 bucket and the keys are rotated after use.
[10:07] Jason: ok, that sounds promising. what's the compliance model for that? we need a paper trail.
[10:12] Luca: every JIT event is an audit event with actor, approvers, time window and rationale; we can export that as a signed artifact for your records.
[10:21] (crosstalk)
[10:26] Maya: i want to highlight the Private deployment option: if you require full network isolation, Private gives you a customer-managed control plane; we can install on-prem or in a VPC. in that mode, keys and data never leave your network unless explicitly configured.
[10:40] Amir: what about upgrades/patching for Private? how do we handle OS/kernel patches?
[10:44] Luca: we provide an upgrade schedule with tested bundles; patches can be applied via our admin tooling with optional maintenance windows. we also provide an air-gapped install bundle for locked environments.
[10:57] Priya: can we test the redaction classifier with our data before going live?
[11:01] Maya: yes — we can run a PII sandbox where you post sanitized/hashed sample prompts and we run the classifier to show findings. that’s part of the pilot.
[11:10] Jason: are there any gotchas — like certain model families that break redaction or return PII in completions?
[11:16] Luca: models can sometimes surface tokens that look like PII if prompts include them; our redaction pipeline runs on request persistence, not on model output. if you want post-response redaction we can enable output filtering as well, but that adds latency.
[11:31] Priya: how do you handle downstream traces — e.g., if we log request ids to our own backend, how do we correlate with Redwood's telemetry without exposing content?
[11:39] Luca: we emit a stable request_id and hashed identifiers. you can store the request_id on your side and link to aggregated telemetry; raw payloads will be redacted per your policy.
[11:49] Amir: can you show the policy JSON for a route? we want to include it in our IaC.
[11:54] Luca: yes — sample policy: 
{
  "route": "fraud-check",
  "retention_days": 7,
  "retention_mode": "redacted",
  "redaction_rules": ["PII-default", "credit-card-12-16"],
  "enforce": true
}

Luca: you can POST this to /v1/policies via the Management API or declare via the Console IaC export.
[12:20] Jason: good. do you support Terraform provider?
[12:23] Maya: yes, we have an official Terraform provider in beta for policy, keys, and role mapping.
[12:29] Priya: what kind of logging is available for performance debugging without revealing content? e.g. stack traces, tokenization artifacts.
[12:37] Luca: you can enable diagnostic logs that include tokenization metrics, model internal errors, and memory/kern traces. those logs are redacted for PII by default; if you need unredacted access you must use the JIT workflow.
[12:52] (short silence)
[13:00] Amir: one more question on retention: if we set redaction then shorten retention to 7 days, do you have delete guarantees? is deletion immediate across all replicas?
[13:09] Luca: we perform coordinated deletes across replicas within a window; we provide a deletion certificate that includes the object ids and timestamps. there is a short propagation window (typically under 5 minutes) to ensure consistency across CDNs and backups. for highly regulated deletes we offer a hard-delete workflow that also purges backups in the next backup cycle.
[13:31] Priya: can you include that deletion certificate in our audit exports?
[13:35] Luca: yes we can.
[13:38] Jason: what about legal holds? sometimes legal asks to pause deletion for a case.
[13:44] Maya: we support legal hold flags at route or account level; when a hold is active deletion is blocked and an explanatory audit entry is created. you can release a hold via an approval flow.
[13:57] Priya: awesome.
[14:00] (luca shares a link to a short demo video in chat) https://redwood.ai/s/console-retention-demo
[14:05] Priya: thanks, we'll watch.
[14:08] Amir: what's the plan for the pilot? we want to test two routes: support-chat (90d redacted) and fraud-check (7d redacted, deterministic hashes).
[14:17] Maya: proposed pilot steps: 1) send security docs and example IaC, 2) provision trial tenant with Dedicated routing for fraud-check, 3) run benchmarking and Optimize evals on your prompt set, 4) 2-week check-in to review metrics.
[14:32] Priya: sounds good. timeline?
[14:35] Maya: we can have the tenant ready by 2026-08-10 and schedule the benchmark week of 2026-08-17.
[14:42] Jason: ok please also include a cost estimate for the dedicated pool for expected QPS.
[14:46] Maya: noted — we’ll include cost modeling.
[14:49] (participants exchange small talk)
[15:00] Priya: quick note — we also evaluate Anthropic for safety controls; would be helpful to see a short comparison doc if you have one.
[15:08] Maya: we can provide a neutral feature matrix comparing retention controls and deployment models; will include that.
[15:15] Jason: final question — are there limits on number of redaction rules or complexity?
[15:20] Luca: no hard limit — we advise grouping and using classifiers for scale; very large regex sets can add CPU overhead. we can run performance tests on your rule set.
[15:32] Amir: that was comprehensive — thanks.
[15:35] Maya: thanks everyone. quick recap of next steps in chat and action items.
[15:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and filler words retained; some product names may be slightly off (KV cash instead of KV cache in a few places).
